forecasts.reason: E007 time scales with epochs; 0.5 epoch cut gives about 5% time and about 0.3 pp loss, leaving it near the 0.753 bar.
Lower final LR likely adds a little accuracy at no time cost, but EMA overlaps with it so the gain is probably under 0.4 pp.
Time saving follows pixel count, but 20 px training likely costs 0.5-1 pp and probably drops below the bar.
Narrowing the last group saves about 3-4% of FLOPs, with a small accuracy loss.
Held-out seeds should give a mean close to 0.759, with a per-seed std of about 0.25 pp.
Launch overhead is already small at batch 2000, and graph capture with Muon and per-resolution shapes is risky; the gain is likely 0-8%.
EMA'd BN buffers are already averaged, so recomputing them probably adds less than 0.3 pp for about 0.1 s.

cruxes: How much accuracy does each lower-resolution epoch cost (slope in pp per pixel-fraction)? This sets how far the resolution schedule can go.
What is the per-seed std, and is the 3-seed mean biased relative to held-out seeds?
What share of the roughly 7.3 s is fixed cost (data transfer, whitening, first-step, EMA) rather than epoch-proportional?
